2. Exact zero detection and rational heights

These parts of the full contract can be handled completely.

Write

$$A_{ij}=\frac{p_{ij}}{q_{ij}},
\qquad p_{ij}\ge0,\quad q_{ij}\ge1,$$

and let $B_A$ denote the total bit length of these explicitly supplied integers. Fractions need not be reduced.

Exact zero detection

Construct the bipartite support graph with edge $ij$ precisely when $p_{ij}>0$. Nonnegativity gives

$$\operatorname{per}(A)=0
\iff
\text{the support graph has no perfect matching}.$$

A deterministic augmenting-path algorithm decides this in polynomial work. In that case, return $L=U=0$. There is no numerical zero threshold.

The exact answer has polynomial rational height

Set

$$D=\prod_{i,j}q_{ij},
\qquad
P=D\,\operatorname{per}(A).$$

Then $P$ is an integer. A permutation’s contribution to $P$ is

$$\left(\prod_i p_{i,\pi(i)}\right)
\left(\prod_{(i,j)\notin\{(i,\pi(i)):i\in[n]\}}q_{ij}\right).$$

Each product uses at most one of the supplied numerator or denominator factors at every matrix position. Consequently,

$$D<2^{B_A},
\qquad
0\le P<n!\,2^{B_A}.$$

Thus both integers in the exact representation $P/D$ have

$$O(B_A+n\log(n+1))$$

bits.

This establishes that output length itself does not obstruct the requested algorithm. It does not provide a polynomial-time way to compute $P$.
